category: per-GB rotating and sticky residential proxy

free_tier.stated: No free allowance on the pricing page. Regular residential packs: 5 GB at $6 on the first recharge only (list $12, $2.4/GB); 20 GB $24, 50 GB $55, 100 + 20 GB $100, 200 GB $180, 500 GB at $350 (list $480); the Regular/Business tabs show $0.55/GB. Purchased traffic does not expire.
free_tier.notes: The metered direction (downloaded versus both ways) is not stated on the page; downloaded-bytes is the nearest term and is unverified.

per_object_cap.stated: not applicable: an address or a traffic pack, not an object

retention.stated: purchased traffic is valid indefinitely: "your purchased traffic is valid indefinitely".
retention.notes: The vendor states no expiry for purchased traffic; days is null because nothing is deleted.

egress.terms: GB-based billing, SOCKS5/HTTP(S), "Unlimited Bandwidth & Concurrency", unlimited IP extraction; the unit sold is traffic.

interface_detail: SOCKS5 and HTTP(S) endpoints; sticky sessions of 1 to 180 minutes or rotation on every request; filtering by country, state, province or city. The vendor supports reseller sub-accounts through CDKey and API; a general API was not otherwise read.
tooling: Any client that speaks SOCKS5 or an HTTP proxy, reached from a Worker through a relay that dials SOCKS5. No SDK was seen on the pages read.
chaining: A rotating residential pool: the upstream sees a different home address per request or per sticky session of up to 180 minutes. The pool is sold as real residential broadband IPs; the registration class of a delivered address was not looked up. A different address is not a different registration class.

limits.value: traffic bought by the GB: 5 GB at $6 on the first recharge only (list $12); 500 GB at $350 (list $480); purchased traffic does not expire
none stated: Unlimited Bandwidth & Concurrency and unlimited IP extraction

binding_note: Bytes are the unit sold, so the price per GB is what binds: $0.70 per GB at the 500 GB pack and $1.20 per GB at the 5 GB pack.

identity_cost.detail: The register page asks for an email address, a verification code sent to it ("Send Code"), a password and agreement to terms, and also offers Sign up with Google. No phone, card or ID document is asked on that page.

reliability_note: The vendor states 99.8% connectivity and a response time under 0.3 s for its residential pool; no measurement was made here.
confidence_note: Price table, protocols, non-expiry and the registration form are read from vendor pages on 2026-11-03. No traffic was bought, so the pool, speed and registration class are unmeasured.
price_per_tb_month: not applicable: sold by the GB with no monthly term; USD 0.7 per GB at the 500 GB pack (USD 350) and USD 1.2 per GB at the 5 GB pack (USD 6)
notes: Named on the Chinese-language forum source as a vendor giving away 500M of residential traffic; the forum is the lead and the evidence is the vendor page. The page title also names datacenter proxies.

extras.rung_note: A rotating pool changes address, not registration class, so it defeats rung 2 and at most rung 3, not rung 5 by assertion alone.
